title: Audit the two-fragment caller’s physical contacts and complete invoice (no new κ)
body:
Independently reconstruct #6726's 7,488 physical contacts and full finite invoice, using parity evaluations and coordinate-decomposition routes without importing its verifier. Replays all 771 arbitrary native input rows, ownership lifetimes, fresh-field handoffs and both boundaries of every canonical job. This complements the scalar endpoint audit in #6733.

The exact bill is 13,670 productive fields, 66,852 paid requests and rank surplus 760. Explicitly decomposing the scattered-coordinate adapters gives a sufficient ordinary bound 535,415,008 < 10^9 under the retained elementary-map rate. No whole 153-axis map is charged as a single small adapter.

Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a.
#6726 source: 435bbe91fb28cb1d7a569ca70c6c4e9eb302d486.
#6733 corroborating endpoint audit: 403b4ed85eea7f99b0c4b4afad22123363492c7a.
Exact inputs, Git/SHA256 pins and their retained ancestor are in SOURCES.json.

Reproduce (CPython 3.12, stdlib):
```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-fragment-physical-invoice-audit
```
Expected: PASS_INDEPENDENT_PR6726_PHYSICAL_INVOICE and PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE.

Executed normal/-O and registered replay; ten mutants reject missing phases/adapters, helper aliasing, omitted paid work, bad fresh-target credit, premature cuts, wrong native charts and corrupted histograms. Separate proof/count review, committed-byte checks and publication-pin replay pass. The complete remote tree equals the tested tree.

No new κ. This is finite application evidence, not scientific admission. Scalar caller endpoints, native physical adapters and the five selected framework assumptions remain inherited. Compiler/outer qualification and physical movement/tape rates remain separate obligations. No selected cold-replay or full-history-preflight PASS is claimed.

By @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance and separate review. Credit zxv (#6726), thu-nmrc (#6716), DreamingOfClouds (#6702), and the complete preserved native/caller lineage. Apache-2.0.
